questions.question: A variety of coal containing approximately 70% carbon is known as: (FBISE 2024-II)
questions.explanation: Coal grades are categorized by carbon content: Peat (~60% C), Lignite (~70% C), Bituminous (~80% C), and Anthracite (~90% C).

questions.question: Which German chemist synthesized urea in 1828, decisively overthrowing the Vital Force Theory? (FBISE 2020-I, 2023-II)
questions.explanation: Friedrich Wöhler disproved the vital force theory in 1828 by heating inorganic ammonium cyanate ($NH_4CNO$) to produce the organic compound urea ($NH_2CONH_2$) in a laboratory.

questions.question: The self-linking ability of carbon atoms through covalent bonds to form long open chains or rings is known as: (FBISE 2018-I, 2022-II)
questions.explanation: Catenation is the remarkable property of carbon atoms to form stable, strong covalent bonds with one another, generating endless varieties of straight, branched, and cyclic molecular skeletons.

questions.question: The functional group characteristic of aldehydes is: (FBISE 2019-II, 2023-I)
questions.explanation: Aldehydes contain the formyl group ($-CHO$), which consists of a carbonyl carbon atom bonded to at least one hydrogen atom and an alkyl/aryl group.

questions.question: Which of the following functional groups imparts a distinctive pleasant, fruity fragrance to organic compounds? (FBISE 2017-I, 2021-II)
questions.explanation: Esters ($-COOR$) are widely recognized for their sweet, fruity aromas and are commonly used as artificial flavorings and in perfumes.

questions.question: In the destructive distillation of coal, what thick, black, viscous liquid containing over 200 aromatic compounds is collected? (FBISE 2016-II, 2022-I)
questions.explanation: Coal tar is the condensed black liquid byproduct of destructive distillation that contains numerous useful aromatic compounds including benzene, toluene, phenol, and naphthalene.

questions.question: What is the primary gaseous hydrocarbon found in natural gas, comprising approximately 85% of its total volume? (FBISE 2015-I, 2020-II)
questions.explanation: Natural gas is composed primarily of methane ($CH_4$, ~85%), along with smaller fractions of ethane, propane, and butane.

questions.question: Successive members in any homologous series differ from each other by a molecular mass of: (FBISE 2014-II, 2021-I)
questions.explanation: Adjacent members of a homologous series differ by one methylene group ($-CH_2-$), which has a formula mass of $12 (C) + 2 (H) = 14\text{ amu}$.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of compounds are functional group isomers? (FBISE 2018-II)
questions.explanation: Ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$, an alcohol) and dimethyl ether ($CH_3OCH_3$, an ether) share the identical molecular formula $C_2H_6O$ but belong to different homologous families due to different functional groups.

questions.question: The superior grade of coal containing 90% or more carbon is: (FBISE 2019-I)
questions.explanation: Anthracite is the hardest and highest metamorphic grade of coal, containing 90% or more carbon, and burns with a hot, clean, smokeless blue flame.

questions.question: What is the general molecular formula for monohydric aliphatic alcohols? (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: Monohydric aliphatic alcohols consist of an alkyl group ($C_nH_{2n+1}-$) attached to a hydroxyl group ($-OH$), giving the general formula $C_nH_{2n+1}OH$ or $C_nH_{2n+2}O$.

questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds has a carbonyl group ($>C=O$) bonded to two alkyl groups? (FBISE 2016-I)
questions.explanation: Ketones contain a carbonyl group ($>C=O$) where the carbon atom is directly attached to two carbon-containing alkyl or aryl groups (general formula $R-CO-R'$).

questions.question: Vital Force Theory stated that organic compounds: (FBISE 2015-II)

options.A: Can be synthesized from inorganic minerals in test tubes
options.B: Could only be synthesized within living organisms by a mystical vital force

questions.explanation: The Vital Force Theory, proposed by Berzelius, claimed that organic compounds could never be synthesized from inorganic materials in a laboratory because their formation required a vital force present only in living systems.

questions.question: The residue left behind after the destructive distillation (carbonization) of coal is known as: (FBISE 2013-I)
questions.explanation: Coke is the solid, porous, high-carbon residue (~98% pure carbon) remaining after volatile matters have been driven off from coal during carbonization.

questions.question: What is the functional group of an ether? (FBISE 2021-I)
questions.explanation: Ethers are characterized by an oxygen atom bonded to two alkyl or aryl groups ($R-O-R'$), known as the alkoxy or ether linkage.

questions.question: Compounds having identical molecular formulas but different arrangements of the carbon skeleton (chain) are called: (FBISE 2023-I)
questions.explanation: Chain isomerism arises from differences in the branching or arrangement of the carbon atom framework (e.g., n-pentane, isopentane, and neopentane).

questions.question: How many structural chain isomers exist for butane ($C_4H_{10}$)?
questions.explanation: Butane ($C_4H_{10}$) has exactly two structural isomers: n-butane ($CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$) and isobutane ($CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$ or 2-methylpropane).

questions.question: How many structural isomers are possible for pentane ($C_5H_{12}$)?
questions.explanation: Pentane ($C_5H_{12}$) has exactly three structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary amine functional group?
questions.explanation: The amino group ($-NH_2$) attached to a carbon atom characterizes primary aliphatic amines ($R-NH_2$), which are derivatives of ammonia.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of the functional group $-COOH$?
questions.explanation: The carboxyl group ($-COOH$) is a combination of a carbonyl group ($>C=O$) and a hydroxyl group ($-OH$), characteristic of carboxylic acids like acetic acid.

questions.question: Which property is NOT generally typical of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Most organic compounds are covalent molecules held together by relatively weak intermolecular forces, which gives them low melting and boiling points compared to ionic compounds.

questions.question: Carbon is tetravalent because:

options.A: It has 4 electrons in its outermost valence shell
options.B: It forms ionic bonds with 4 halogen atoms
options.D: It has 4 protons in its nucleus

questions.explanation: Carbon has an atomic number of 6 with electronic configuration $1s^2 2s^2 2p^2$. With 4 valence electrons, it shares 4 electron pairs to achieve stable noble gas configuration, exhibiting tetravalency.

questions.question: The conversion of wood into coal through biochemical and geological processes over millions of years is termed: (FBISE 2014-I)
questions.explanation: Carbonization is the slow, natural transformation of buried plant and wood deposits into coal in the absence of air under high temperature and geological pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following fractions of petroleum distillation has the lowest boiling range?
questions.explanation: Refinery gas consists of small hydrocarbons ($C_1-C_4$) with boiling points below 20°C, collected from the very top of the fractionating column.

questions.question: The simplest organic compound belonging to the ketone family is:
questions.explanation: Because a carbonyl carbon in a ketone must be bonded to two other carbon atoms, the smallest possible ketone is acetone ($CH_3-CO-CH_3$), having 3 carbon atoms.

questions.question: The simplest member of the carboxylic acid family is:
questions.explanation: Formic acid (methanoic acid, $HCOOH$) is the simplest carboxylic acid, where the carboxyl group is bonded to a single hydrogen atom.

questions.question: A condensed structural formula shows:

options.A: Only the elemental symbols and total counts of each atom
options.B: The groups of atoms in sequence without showing individual single bonds
options.C: All chemical bonds in three dimensions

questions.explanation: A condensed structural formula (such as $CH_3CH_2CH_3$) groups the hydrogen atoms together with their associated carbon atoms in sequence without drawing every individual $C-H$ single bond.

questions.question: 1-chloropropane and 2-chloropropane are examples of:
questions.explanation: Position isomerism occurs when compounds have the same carbon skeleton and functional group, but the functional group is located at different positions on the chain.

questions.question: The general formula for an alkyl radical is:
questions.explanation: An alkyl radical is formed by removing one hydrogen atom from an alkane molecule ($C_nH_{2n+2} - H = C_nH_{2n+1}-$), represented by the symbol $R-$.

questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds is a heterocyclic compound?
questions.explanation: Pyridine ($C_5H_5N$) is a cyclic organic compound where the ring contains one nitrogen atom in addition to carbon atoms, making it heterocyclic.

questions.question: Ammoniacal liquor obtained during destructive distillation of coal is treated with sulphuric acid to manufacture:
questions.explanation: Ammoniacal liquor is an aqueous solution of ammonia. When neutralized with sulphuric acid, it crystallizes into the synthetic fertilizer ammonium sulphate: $2NH_3 + H_2SO_4 \to (NH_4)_2SO_4$.

questions.question: Which type of coal has the highest moisture content and lowest carbon percentage?
questions.explanation: Peat represents the initial stage in coal formation. It has a low carbon content (~60%) and high moisture content, producing substantial smoke when burned.

questions.question: A functional group is best defined as:

options.A: An atom or group of atoms that imparts characteristic chemical properties to an organic molecule
options.B: The total number of carbon atoms in a chain
options.C: Any non-metal present in an organic compound
options.D: The solvent in which the compound dissolves

questions.explanation: A functional group is an atom or group of atoms whose presence dictates the distinctive chemical reactivity and physical behavior of an organic family.

questions.question: Which of the following functional groups contains a nitrogen atom directly bonded to a carbonyl group?
questions.explanation: The amide functional group consists of a carbonyl carbon atom bonded directly to an amino nitrogen atom ($-CO-NH_2$ or $-CO-NHR$).

questions.question: The general molecular formula of alkyl halides is:
questions.explanation: Alkyl halides (haloalkanes) are formed by replacing one hydrogen atom of an alkane with a halogen atom ($X = F, Cl, Br, I$), represented by $C_nH_{2n+1}X$ or $R-X$.
